headline: Curated microbial reference resources and reproducible genome analysis tooling advance
label: Microbial Profiling And Genome Tooling
summary: New 16S and mOTUs reference resources plus workflow tools for nanopore 16S outputs, pairwise genome alignment and annotation scoring appeared this week.
synthesis: The dominant thread is improving microbial taxonomic profiling through curated reference data and interoperable tooling, alongside reproducible comparative-genomics workflows. The mOTUs-db update links microbial taxonomy to genome-encoded function and environmental and geographic distributions, exposing profiling through a CLI and API. RADSuite targets species-level resolution in 16S studies by pairing RADlib, a curated 16S rRNA gene copy database, with RADx, which identifies the variable regions sequenced. VPHYL, an R Shiny app, converts Emu and EPI2ME wf-16s nanopore 16S abundance tables into phyloseq or BIOM objects with automated HTML reports, bridging long-read outputs to standard downstream ecosystems. On the genome side, nf-core/pairgenomealign wraps LAST pairwise whole-genome alignment in a scalable Nextflow pipeline with standard output formats and benchmarking. ABAQS scores annotation quality via completeness, gene model validity and protein profile accuracy, applied to over 1700 fungal genomes. Scopes differ, and the summaries do not support cross-tool performance comparisons.
